v2.text: A 53 year old woman with metastatic pancreatic cancer sustained a traumatic fracture of her right humerus. Prior to the injury, she was taking hydromorphone {{pre_dose_6hr}} mg every 6 hours. She underwent ORIF of her right humerus, and by postoperative day 2, she was taking hydromorphone {{post_oral_dose_4hr}} mg PO every 4 hours and additional hydromorphone {{post_iv_dose_4hr}} mg IV every 4 hours. Convert her total current hydromorphone administration as of postoperative day 2 to entirely PO dosing in order to begin an opioid taper plan.  How many mg/4hr of hydromorphone should she receive orally?

v3.text: Before her recent accident, a 53-year-old woman living with metastatic pancreatic cancer relied on hydromorphone {{pre_dose_6hr}} mg taken every six hours for chronic pain. After a traumatic break of the right humerus and subsequent ORIF, her analgesic needs changed significantly. By the second day after surgery, her pain management consisted of two overlapping schedules: oral hydromorphone {{post_oral_dose_4hr}} mg every four hours and an additional intravenous dose of {{post_iv_dose_4hr}} mg at the same frequency. To design a tapering strategy, translate the entirety of her current hydromorphone intake on postoperative day two into an equivalent all-oral regimen. What oral hydromorphone dose every four hours would match her total present usage?

v4.text: A 61-year-old woman with advanced ovarian carcinoma had been maintained on hydromorphone {{pre_dose_6hr}} mg every six hours for chronic pain. She later developed a severe left femoral injury that required operative repair. On the second day after surgery, her analgesic regimen consisted of hydromorphone {{post_oral_dose_4hr}} mg taken orally every four hours, supplemented by {{post_iv_dose_4hr}} mg of intravenous hydromorphone at the same interval. To prepare for a structured dose-reduction plan, convert the total hydromorphone she is receiving on postoperative day two into an entirely oral schedule. What oral hydromorphone dose should she receive every four hours?

v5.text: A 41-year-old patient with advanced colon cancer had been using hydromorphone {{pre_dose_6hr}} mg every six hours as part of her chronic pain regimen. On the second day after the procedure, her pain control consisted of hydromorphone {{post_oral_dose_4hr}} mg taken orally every four hours, supplemented with {{post_iv_dose_4hr}} mg administered intravenously at the same interval. To initiate a structured taper, convert the full amount of hydromorphone she is receiving on postoperative day two into an equivalent all-oral schedule. How many milligrams of hydromorphone should she receive by mouth every four hours?
